title: Pressure-induced concurrent amorphization and superconductivity in topological material NbNiTe5
authors: Lingxiao Zhao, Yi Zhao, Bangshuai Zhu, Qi Wang, Cuiying Pei, Juefei Wu, Jin-Ke Bao, Wen-He Jiao, Yanpeng Qi
abstract: We have systematically studied the structural and electronic properties of a topological material NbNiTe5 under high pressure. The evolution of the normal state resistance shows a non-monotonic trend from 0.7 GPa to 5.1 GPa, in accordance with the second-order transition along the inter-layer direction observed in X-ray diffraction and Raman spectra. At around 10 GPa, the sample starts amorphization, which is concurrent with the emergence of superconductivity. Upon further compression, the structural disorder enhances and the superconducting transition becomes clearer, suggesting that the superconductivity is modulated by the degree of disorder in NbNiTe5 under high pressure. Within 45.7 GPa, the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) slowly rises from 0.6 K at 9.5 GPa to 1.4 K at 45.7 GPa. Our findings extend the family of transition metal chalcogenide superconductors and shed new light on understanding superconductivity in disordered systems.
summary: This work reports that applying high pressure causes the topological material $	ext{NbNiTe}_5$ to undergo amorphization, which coincides with the onset of superconductivity. Crucially, the superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$) is found to increase as the structural disorder increases during compression, suggesting disorder plays a key role in enhancing pairing mechanisms.
main_problem: The study investigates the unusual relationship between pressure-induced structural disorder (amorphization) and the emergence/enhancement of superconductivity in a topological material.
main_result: Superconductivity emerges concurrently with amorphization around 10 GPa, and the superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$) progressively increases as the degree of structural disorder enhances up to 45.7 GPa.
method: The research combines high-pressure electrical transport measurements, in-situ X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, and theoretical modeling (DFT) to track material changes under compression.
model_or_system: The physical system is the topological transition metal chalcogenide $	ext{NbNiTe}_5$. The study examines its structural evolution from crystalline to amorphous states under extreme pressure.
key_observables: Superconducting Transition Temperature ($T_c$), normal state resistance, upper critical field ($\mu_0H_{c2}$), and lattice parameter changes observed via XRD/Raman.
important_parameters: Pressure (up to 45.7 GPa); temperature; structural disorder level.
main_assumptions: The enhancement of $T_c$ is directly modulated by the degree of structural disorder induced by high pressure, suggesting a mechanism related to disorder-enhanced electron-phonon coupling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate resistance evolution showing superconductivity onset; XRD/Raman spectra track lattice changes and amorphization; phase diagrams map $T_c$ vs. pressure alongside structural transitions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents evidence: initial normal state behavior $ightarrow$ observation of structural transition (amorphization) $ightarrow$ confirmation of superconductivity onset coinciding with disorder $ightarrow$ quantitative measurement of $T_c$ enhancement across the disordered regime.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the core mechanism—how controlled structural disorder enhances a quantum phenomenon like superconductivity—is highly relevant to understanding strongly correlated and disordered quantum systems.
